claim: You can detach an EBS volume explicitly or by terminating the instance, but if the instance is running you must first unmount the volume; a volume detached without unmounting can lose in-progress writes.
question: What must you do before you detach an EBS volume from a running instance?

values.display: you must first unmount the volume
the data on the volume might be out of sync

evidence.quote: You can detach an Amazon EBS volume from an instance explicitly or by terminating the instance. However, if the instance is running, you must first unmount the volume from the instance.
If there were writes to the volume in progress when it was detached, the data on the volume might be out of sync.

claim: To detach a volume that is the root device of an instance, you must stop the instance first.
question: Can you detach the root EBS volume of a running instance?

values.display: you must stop the instance
the root device of an instance

evidence.quote: If an EBS volume is the root device of an instance, you must stop the instance before you can detach the volume.

claim: New volumes are raw block devices and need a file system before you can mount and use them; volumes created from snapshots likely already have one, and creating a new file system on top overwrites the data.
question: Must you create a file system on an EBS volume before using it?

values.display: you must create a file system on them
the operation overwrites your data

evidence.quote: New volumes are raw block devices, and you must create a file system on them before you can mount and use them. Volumes that were created from snapshots likely have a file system on them already; if you create a new file system on top of an existing file system, the operation overwrites your data.

claim: After you increase the size of a volume, you must also extend the volume's partition and file system to use the additional storage capacity.
question: After you grow an EBS volume with Elastic Volumes, is the extra space usable at once inside the operating system?

values.display: you must also extend the volume's partition
to make use of the additional storage capacity

evidence.quote: If you've increased the size of your volume, then you must also extend the volume's partition to make use of the additional storage capacity.

claim: Modifying a volume's configuration has no charge; you are charged for the new configuration from the moment the modification starts.
question: Does it cost anything to modify an EBS volume, and when does the new price apply?

values.display: There is no charge to modify the configuration
after volume modification starts

evidence.quote: There is no charge to modify the configuration of a volume. You are charged for the new volume configuration after volume modification starts.

claim: A root volume of type io1, io2, gp2, gp3 or standard cannot be modified to an st1 or sc1 volume, even when it is detached.
question: Can you change a root EBS volume to st1 or sc1?

values.display: can't be modified to an st1 or sc1 volume
even if it is detached from the instance

evidence.quote: A root volume of type io1, io2, gp2, gp3, or standard can't be modified to an st1 or sc1 volume, even if it is detached from the instance.

claim: When EBS finds a volume's data potentially inconsistent, by default it disables I/O to the volume from attached instances to prevent corruption, and the volume status becomes impaired; the Auto-Enable IO attribute overrides this.
question: What does EBS do by default when a volume status check finds potentially inconsistent data?

values.display: disables I/O to the volume
the volume status is impaired
configuring the volume to automatically enable I/O

evidence.quote: When Amazon EBS determines that a volume's data is potentially inconsistent, the default is that it disables I/O to the volume from any attached EC2 instances, which helps to prevent data corruption. After I/O is disabled, the next volume status check fails, and the volume status is impaired.

If the consistency of a particular volume is not a concern, and you'd prefer that the volume be made available immediately if it's impaired, you can override the default behavior by configuring the volume to automatically enable I/O.

claim: The I/O performance status check compares actual volume performance to expected performance and is available only for io1, io2 and gp3 volumes attached to an instance.
question: Which EBS volume types have the I/O performance status check?

values.display: compares actual volume performance to the expected performance
Provisioned IOPS SSD (io1 and io2) and General Purpose SSD (gp3)

evidence.quote: The I/O performance status check compares actual volume performance to the expected performance of a volume. It alerts you if the volume is performing below expectations. This status check is available only for Provisioned IOPS SSD (io1 and io2) and General Purpose SSD (gp3) volumes that are attached to an instance.

claim: All EBS volume types automatically send 1-minute metrics to CloudWatch at no charge, but only while the volume is attached to an instance.
question: Do EBS volumes send CloudWatch metrics by default, at what period and cost?

values.display: 1-minute periods at no charge
only when the volume is attached to an instance

evidence.quote: Data is available automatically in 1-minute periods at no charge.
All Amazon EBS volume types automatically send 1-minute metrics to CloudWatch, but only when the volume is attached to an instance.

claim: On instances built on the Nitro System, EBS volumes are exposed as NVMe block devices; the device names the operating system uses can differ from, or come in a different order than, the names in the block device mapping.
question: How does a Nitro-based instance see its EBS volumes, and does the OS device name match the name given in EC2?

values.display: exposed as NVMe block devices
in a different order than you specified
can be different than the name

evidence.quote: Amazon EBS volumes are exposed as NVMe block devices on Amazon EC2 instances built on the AWS Nitro System.
The block device driver can assign NVMe device names in a different order than you specified for the volumes in the block device mapping.
The block device driver for the instance assigns the actual volume name when mounting the volume, and the name assigned can be different than the name that Amazon EC2 uses.

claim: Multi-Attach can be enabled or disabled after volume creation, but not while the volume is attached to an instance, and it cannot be enabled during instance launch.
question: Can you turn on Multi-Attach for an existing volume, and when?

values.display: You can't enable or disable Multi-Attach
can't be enabled during instance launch

qualifiers.scope: Multi-Attach on io1 and io2 volumes
qualifiers.condition: the volume must not be attached

evidence.quote: You can't enable or disable Multi-Attach while the volume is attached to an instance.
Multi-Attach can't be enabled during instance launch using either the Amazon EC2 console or RunInstances API.

claim: Each instance attached to a Multi-Attach volume can drive up to the volume's maximum provisioned performance, but the combined performance of all attached instances cannot exceed it.
question: Is a Multi-Attach volume's provisioned IOPS shared by all attached instances?

values.display: the aggregate performance of all of the attached instances
can't exceed the volume's maximum provisioned performance

evidence.quote: Each attached instance is able to drive its maximum IOPS performance up to the volume's maximum provisioned performance. However, the aggregate performance of all of the attached instances can't exceed the volume's maximum provisioned performance.

claim: For a Multi-Attach enabled volume, the only supported type change is between io1 and io2, in either direction and even while attached.
question: Which volume type changes are allowed on a Multi-Attach enabled volume?

values.display: between io1 and io2 in either direction
Other volume type changes are not supported

evidence.quote: For Multi-Attach enabled volumes, you can change the volume type between io1 and io2 in either direction, including while the volume is attached. Other volume type changes are not supported.

claim: A Multi-Attach enabled volume with an issue at the EBS infrastructure layer is unavailable to all attached instances, while EC2 or network issues may affect only some of them.
question: Does Multi-Attach protect against a failure of the EBS volume itself?

values.display: unavailable to all attached instances
might impact only some attached instances

evidence.quote: Multi-Attach enabled volumes that have an issue at the Amazon EBS infrastructure layer are unavailable to all attached instances. Issues at the Amazon EC2 or networking layer might impact only some attached instances.

claim: There is no additional charge for EBS Multi-Attach; you pay the standard charges of the io1 or io2 volume.
question: Does EBS Multi-Attach cost extra?

values.display: There are no additional charges
the standard charges that apply

evidence.quote: There are no additional charges for using Amazon EBS Multi-Attach. You are billed the standard charges that apply to Provisioned IOPS SSD (io1 and io2) volumes.
